version: PRD Rev D (Phase 4 real-data test, November 2026)
note: Alert thresholds for a crewed Mars transit. The team set each value from the cited sources and from a test on measured MSL RAD data. They are not NASA flight rules. The mission team controls the radiation rules in src/data/rules.json. Each crew member can set stricter personal body limits on the Body systems page.

units.factorBasis: MSL RAD cruise: 1.84 mSv/d over 0.481 mGy/d. One factor for the whole demo. It overstates the SPE dose, because SPE protons have a lower quality factor than GCR.

singleSpe.label: NASA SPE limit, design reference event
singleSpe.note: [V1 4031]: the program shall protect crew from the design reference SPE (sum of the October 1989 events) to less than a NASA effective dose of 250 mSv. It is a design requirement for the vehicle. The app shows it for scale only.

shelterGoal.label: Orion shelter design goal for a large event

floorMultiple.label: 10 × B
floorMultiple.basis: Hard floor. 2 or more sensors at 10 × B for 5 min always give a Warning, also when the crew inhibits R-W1. It is the team's first Warning rule.

projection24hMSv.label: 50 mSv in 24 h, unsheltered
projection24hMSv.basis: Team value. A fast rise to this level needs a Warning before the 30 min confirmation ends.

shelterFactor.label: Shelter keeps 25% of the cabin dose rate
shelterFactor.basis: Team value. Orion data (George 2024): a model of the October 1989 SPE gives 0.23 in the storm shelter. The measured inner-belt value is 0.47. If our shelter is like the measured case, the shelter saves 53% of the event dose. The app uses 75%.

timing.note: donkiLookbackMin: how long a flare or CME record keeps an Advisory. cautionFlareWindowMin: how long an X-class flare with a fast CME keeps a Caution. A record that one event used does not start a second event. Team values.

rules.title: Solar activity, no dose rise
triggers: DONKI logs a flare of class M1 or higher.
DONKI logs a CME at 500 km/s or faster.
All sensors stay below 1.25 × B (0.096 mSv/h).
rules.action: Read at the next daily review. No timeline change.
rules.basis: M-class and stronger flares and fast CMEs come before most large proton events. The dose at the vehicle is still normal.

rules.title: Sensor does not agree
triggers: 1 sensor reads at or above 3 × B (0.23 mSv/h) and the other sensors do not agree.
The personal dosimeter and the cabin mean differ by more than 25% for 10 min.
A sensor sends no data for 5 min.
rules.action: Check the sensor. Read the personal dosimeter. No shelter action.
rules.basis: One sensor alone is often a fault, not an event. This rule stops a single bad sensor from giving a Caution or a Warning.

rules.title: Solar particle event likely
triggers: DONKI logs an SEP event (≥10 MeV at ≥10 pfu, NOAA S1).
DONKI logs a flare of class X1 or higher with a linked CME at 1,000 km/s or faster.
2 or more sensors read at or above 1.5 × B (0.12 mSv/h) for 30 min.
rules.action: Finish or safe the task within 30 min. Stage the shelter. Put the vest within reach.
rules.basis: Fast CMEs drive the largest proton events. Two sensors that agree give a real rise, not a fault. 30 min is enough to safe most tasks.

rules.title: Solar particle event
triggers: 2 or more sensors read at or above 2 × B (0.15 mSv/h) for 30 min.
The projected unsheltered dose for the next 24 h is 50 mSv or more.
rules.action: Go to the shelter now. Start procedure SH-1.
rules.basis: Phase 4 test on 6 real events measured by MSL RAD (2012 cruise, 2017 and 2024 on Mars): this rule sheltered before the peak in 6 of 6 events with 0 false entries. The old rule (10 × B for 5 min) missed 4 of 6. Each hour of delay in a fast event costs 3 to 10 percentage points of the event dose. NASA asks for doses as low as reasonably achievable (ALARA).
